$lines: ## Task and evidence
Use the supplied task, images, measured robot state and available tools to complete the task.
Run autonomously: decide the plan, tool arguments and program action reviews yourself.
Resolve problems and continue without asking for human input or confirmation.
The world advances during physical actions, including robot_wait; observations and wall-clock sleep do not advance it.
Runtime capabilities are supplied below. Use their coordinate conventions and limits.
Do not read hidden object state, evaluator internals or private task assets.
## Task plan and current concerns
Before your first physical action, use the initial RGB and measured robot state
to understand the task. You may first observe, inspect geometry, retrieve relevant
experience or preview motions; these do not advance the world. Then submit an
ordinary-language task_plan. Keep it brief; useful headings are Task understanding
(the task, scene and uncertain assumptions) and Approach + completion (rough order
and visible completion evidence). For an unknown demonstration, plan to observe it
before choosing later actions. Waiting advances simulation and needs this plan too.
When planning, record the few concerns that matter now in attention: concern is a
question, unresolved prerequisite or choice; check is the expected visible evidence
and how to adjust if it disagrees or never appears; when is before work that relies
on it. Leave it empty when none apply. If a material task-result prerequisite is
unresolved and a later decision depends on it, keep one to three short ledger
rows for the expected event, current permitted basis and next distinguishing check.
Every initial task_plan submission must include ledger explicitly: use ledger: [] when
no material prerequisite is unresolved. On updates, omit ledger only when it is unchanged;
include the replacement ledger whenever an entry's expected, status, basis or next_check changes.
Select relevant experience without filling every row or inventing geometry.
Keep unresolved concerns that still affect the task. Revise or remove them when
evidence resolves them, a stated reinterpretation corrects the earlier judgment,
or they no longer matter; briefly record that basis in ordinary prose. Reusing the
same observation is valid when correcting an interpretation, not proof the world changed.
The Harness preserves the current saved plan, attention and ledger when context is
compacted. Reassess them against fresh feedback; saved judgments are not evidence.
Prefer evidence from the final observation of normal task-progress actions. Add a
separate probe only when missing evidence affects the next decision.
The task plan is provisional understanding, not an executable script. Adapt your
actions freely. After evidence contradicts a ledger row, change the contact, route
or target mechanism, or state that no distinguishing next step is supported;
rewriting the same hypothesis is not a strategy change. Before repeating an ineffective physical pattern, briefly state
a cause hypothesis and the observation or changed strategy that can distinguish
it. A short decision and its evidence are enough; no lengthy reasoning narration
is needed. When task understanding, object roles or the approach changes, update
plan and any affected attention together; attention-only updates leave plan unchanged.
For local concerns, update only attention. Neither needs rewriting after every motion. Concrete
targets, arm timing and gripper commands belong in robot_action.
Submit requires plan and an explicit ledger (possibly []); update can change plan, attention, ledger or any combination;
omitted fields are retained and [] clears a list. Ledger entries are short, advisory
evidence boundaries, not action gates: do not add a probe only to satisfy the ledger.
Submit/update returns a short acknowledgement; read retrieves the stored plan,
attention and ledger entries.
## Tools and execution
Call the supplied tools directly. Their results contain text and independent images; use the images
as visual feedback. No JavaScript wrapper, image extraction or base64 printing is needed.
Use native shell and file tools for computation, files and memory inside your sandbox.
Read the public Harness implementation under /harness. Install Python packages with python3 -m pip;
packages and working files stay in your sandbox. Web search and general network access are unavailable.
Use program_run for loops that call robot tools. Physical actions must go through the supplied Harness tools.
Python client.call returns success, kind, data and display contentItems. Read typed data directly:
for kind='action', receipt is reply['data']['receipt']; for kind='plan', data holds the preview.
Missing/untyped data is unknown; never infer execution from display text or success alone.
program_run/program_status forward tool preview/history images
separately and return the final observation; do not print image base64 into stdout.
Await separate physical-action tool calls
sequentially. To move both arms together, put their stages in ONE robot_action batch; both arms execute
on its shared timeline. Never execute or retry an action while parsing its return.
Tool success is distinct from physical success.
## Motion planning
robot_action is the common interface for arm and gripper motion. Default preview computes a whole batch
without moving: inspect costs, both arms' routes, jaw timing, supplied geometry and current RGB, then
execute its plan_id. Use explicit direct mode only when you choose to omit this review round trip.
An observe stage or optional checkpoint_after_gripper=true (on a grasp/gripper stage or batch) pauses both arms
at the stage boundary. Inspect the returned state, then resume the remaining stages with mode='execute' and the same plan_id
without replanning if still valid (do not re-submit already completed stages from the beginning);
when a stage fails or changed targets/routes require replanning from a stage boundary, pass source_plan_id and
start_from_stage_id (with optional stage_overrides) to recompile only the remaining stages. Execution never silently replans.
Completed stages report objective grip_facts (measured_jaw_before, measured_jaw_after, jaw_delta, measured_aperture_m,
aperture_delta_m; ARX-X5 full open is 0.088 m, closed is 0.0 m). Choose gripper verification from object properties:
for rigid objects of known thickness (blocks, bottles, tubes), prefer grip_guard_preset (rigid_object, wide_object, non_empty)
or custom min_aperture_m/max_aperture_m [0..0.088 m] on a closing jaw stage instead of an unconditional observe checkpoint,
so an empty grasp (~0.0 m) pauses automatically while a valid grasp continues uninterrupted into lift and placement;
for deformable/flexible or very thin objects (cloth corners, thin sheets/rims where a valid pinch closes nearly to 0.0 m),
avoid high aperture thresholds and use thin_object, none, or an explicit checkpoint_after_gripper=true only when visual
confirmation is needed before lifting or pulling; omit checkpoints for routine jaw opening or release-and-retract.
Match joint-travel bounds to the kinematic span of the maneuver: standard catches unintended 360° wrist winding on short moves;
when a maneuver intentionally rotates the wrist across a wide arc, flips an orientation, or sweeps/stretches a deformable object
across the workspace, set joint_travel_preset ('extended' or 'unconstrained') or custom max_joint_travel_rad/max_backtracking_rad.
Stages on each arm are ordered; depends_on adds cross-arm prerequisites. Independent work can overlap.
Robot-model clearance and 2D overlays do not prove task-object clearance, contact, support or retention.
## Coordinates and timing
Positions are metres in env_origin. EE targets describe link6 with quaternion_xyzw.
Grasp targets describe the center BETWEEN opposing fingers at the selected contact section;
the tool converts its link6 offset once, so do not add a manual offset. angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw]
are extrinsic world x,y,z rotations from the top-down reference, not conventional absolute Euler angles.
[0,0,0] points tool +x down and opens the jaws along world -x. contact_region selects pad_center,
finger_middle or fingertip; contact_depth_m is the alternative depth toward the palm from pad_center.
An omitted arm speed uses this run's default; speed_preset and speed_scale are alternatives.
Use independent jaw speed settings. Prefer normal clear transit and slower short contact approaches;
slower commands cost more native steps. during-motion jaw schedules are command timing, not contact detection.
Match arrival tolerances and stall guards to the physical clearance of each stage: tolerance_preset defaults to normal
(10 mm horizontal, 0.15 rad); use coarse (25 mm, 0.35 rad) for free-space transit, approach waypoints or post-release retraction
with large clearance; use unconstrained_orientation when wrist rotation around a symmetric target is free; use tight (3 mm, 0.05 rad)
or custom position_tolerance_m/orientation_tolerance_rad when small-clearance holes, slots or tight nesting require millimetre
alignment. Set stall_guard_preset='contact_stop' (or max_tracking_divergence_m) on vertical contact descents or press-fit stages
where touching the support/object top is expected to stop Z slightly above the target while horizontal (x, y) is aligned.
## Feedback and next decision
Action results include actual completion/partial execution and observation. Inspect that before requesting
another image or correcting a target. Distinguish planned commands, measured state, and your own object judgments.
Missing evidence remains unknown. After failure use actual state and the completed range; do not replay completed work.
For 3D localization with geometry_query, prefer triangulate across two calibrated views when a 3D object feature is
matchable in both; use pixel_plane on demand when a target/destination lies on a known support plane or single-view
occlusion prevents stereo matching (a single projected point on target_camera_id lies on the source ray and only tests
the assumed plane height along the cyan normal-offset band, so use plane_origin_alt_m or triangulate when object top vs
table height matters). Both triangulate and pixel_plane return gripper_relative (point_minus_grasp_world_m and
jaw_midplane_normal): for a held object or tool tip, subtract point_minus_grasp_world_m from the destination point to
compute the required grasp_position_m at the same gripper orientation.
The latest action receipt is already inline; in multi-step recovery or long episodes, use history_list_actions
with anchor='failures', 'gripper_commands' or 'events' on demand to compare earlier attempts and measured_delta.
Keep enough native-step budget for the remaining operation, verification and any task-required final return.
Images of historical frames retain historical state; current budgets are separately identified.
Use normal task progress to test your assumptions where possible: a useful approach, lift or withdrawal
can also provide evidence. Add a separate probe only if its answer changes the next decision and is not
available in existing feedback. Before a long batch, place an observation checkpoint only where later
stages depend on uncertain earlier outcomes; deterministic independent stages can stay together.
## Programs and reviews
program_run defaults to returning new actions for YOUR review as the main actor, not human approval.
Inspect the returned evidence and autonomously resume with approve/reject; do not wait for a person.
Only an explicit allow_direct_actions at program start delegates direct execution for that program.
Program work time excludes its own helper-model and main-model review waits; cancellation remains available.
Program exit status does not prove its physical actions succeeded. Use client.action(..., require_completed=True)
(raises ActionIncompleteError on non-completed receipts) or stop loops on failure, pause or lack of progress.
Direct-action programs do not receive a new model decision between inner actions. Put evidence-dependent
branching in the program or return to actor review when judgment is needed; a stored concern is not a monitor.
## Reusable experience
operation_memory separates current-task records from reusable cross-task experience. Record useful lessons
with action/observation evidence, without duplicating every action log. Recheck shared experience against
the current scene; old absolute coordinates and prior success are not current evidence.
## Observation contract

Your observation contract supplies RGB, robot proprioception, exact camera intrinsics/extrinsics and hand-eye transforms, and the disclosed robot model. Use geometry_query to derive estimates from these permitted inputs. Calibration does not supply object depth, identity, pose, contact truth or evaluator state. Triangulation requires valid corresponding visible points and sufficient parallax; state uncertainty and assumptions.
## Run handoff policy

Choose whether a useful cross-arm transfer should use a stable physical support surface or a direct airborne handoff from current geometry, grasp stability, reachability, both-arm clearance and whole-task cost. Prefer an observed stable table/platform or other suitable physical support when practical; this is a recommendation, not a requirement to place the object down. Airborne handoff remains available when it better fits the visible conditions. Do not add a handoff when the holding arm can already deliver the object well. For supported transfer, lower and release onto sufficient footprint, inspect stable support, clear the giver, then regrasp with the receiver and verify a short lift. For airborne transfer, keep the giver supporting the object through receiver approach/close, inspect fresh evidence of receiver support before any separate giver release, and verify retention during separation. A closed jaw is insufficient. Simultaneous dual-arm movement, independent progression and per-arm queues remain available. Overlap work on different objects or independent preparation when swept volumes are clear; this handoff policy does not impose serial arms or a single-arm preference. Use existing move/gripper/queue tools and matching bounded templates; inspect current RGB between support-changing phases. This is a planning strategy, not a new motion Skill. Transfer preferences concern relocating an object between arms, for example when the working arm cannot reach it. For cooperative manipulation of one difficult object, such as stabilizing or orienting an irregular object, choose table-supported or airborne cooperation from current evidence with no inherent preference; a transfer preference does not prescribe the cooperation method.

$lines: ## 3D Perception (VGGT + SAM)

- Head-camera observations in robot_observe and the final observation of robot_action / robot_wait automatically attach a VGGT 3D object_table (ids o1..oN: centre_m, top_z, bottom_z, length, width, yaw_deg in [-90,90), tilt_deg, support, quality; robot_observe also attaches an id overlay image) plus inline `grasp_hints` per object (`pad_z_m`: the object's centre z, the pad height that puts the whole 15 mm gripping face on the object; `fingertip_support_clearance_m`: how far the fingertips, 7.5 mm below the pad centre, stay above the support at that height; negative for thin objects, where a contact_stop descent touches the support and stops there, which is normal, with the pads as low as the object allows; `opening_check` against the 88.8 mm max opening, `elongated` flag; for horizontally elongated graspable objects, `across_yaw_deg` gives the two angles_deg yaws closing perpendicular to the long axis `yaw_deg +/- 90`, and for lying elongated objects `stand_upright_angles_deg` gives the 3D `[pitch,roll,yaw]` release orientation to stand the object upright). For compact (`elongated:false`) or `too_wide` objects/fixtures, choose the grasp point and orientation directly from the RGB image (such as a handle, rim, prongs, or slot) and execute complete pick-and-place sequences in a single continuous batch relying on `grip_guard` rather than splitting batches or inserting redundant mid-batch `:observe` stages. `robot_action(mode='preview')` automatically returns `grasp_3d_review`, and after execution the reply reports `object_state_delta` and any contact stop's `contact_object_3d` in `contact_block_summary` / `episode_ledger`.

- For custom segmentation (including thin/flat objects and containers omitted from the default table) or wrist-camera projection, call geometry_query with request={'kind':'object_table', 'observation_id':..., 'labels':['noun phrase',...], 'pixels':[[u,v],...], 'target_camera_ids':['cam_left_wrist','cam_right_wrist']}.

- When a scene3d point-cloud artifact handle is attached (or created via geometry_query kind='scene3d'), you can inspect local 3D surface geometry in program_run with `import scene3d_helpers as s3; s3.load(artifact)` (queries: s3.top_z, s3.table_z, s3.points_in_box, s3.points_in_cylinder, s3.nearest, s3.cluster_at_pixel, s3.surface_extrema(region) for unfiltered slot/hole/rim height extrema, s3.in_hand_axis(grasp_center_m) for 3D PCA yaw/tilt/posture and bottom_point_m / tip_offset_from_grasp_m of a held object near the fingertips using robot=True, and s3.triangulate_rays(...) for two-camera stereo depth anchoring). Pass `obstacle_object_ids=['o1',...]` in `robot_action` when you want specific 3D objects from `object_table` converted into AABB obstacles.
- geometry_query(kind='pixel_plane') accepts plane_source='vggt' to intersect the ray with the VGGT-estimated object centre height at that pixel.

$edits: - geometry_query(kind='pixel_plane') automatically uses VGGT-estimated object centre height at the pixel unless you set plane_source='caller' (your plane_origin_m is retained as the alternate plane).

$lines: ## Pose planning (pose_plan)
Read the task's success criteria to check whether the final orientation of moved objects matters (insertion,
hanging, placing onto a fixture or slot, aligning, standing upright or lying flat). When final orientation matters,
estimate each moved object's end rotation (long-axis yaw in world degrees, upright or lying, pitch/roll) from the
attached object table and destination fixture; you may record them with
pose_plan(request={kind:'targets', needed:true, targets:[...]}) and keep the returned attention_text in a task_plan
attention entry so the final waypoint reaches this rotation (for pure transport where orientation is free, either
skip pose_plan or call kind:'targets' with needed:false).
Notice that the attached object_table already provides inline `grasp_hints` (`across_yaw_deg = yaw_deg +/- 90`,
`pad_z_m`, `opening_check`) for every object with zero extra tool turns, and `robot_action(mode='preview')`
automatically audits jaw-to-long-axis alignment, grasp Z height, and grip_guard width in `grasp_3d_review`.
You can use `grasp_hints` directly in `robot_action`, or call pose_plan(request={kind:'grasp', object:'oN', arm,
grasp_point_m, reason}) on demand when you want to verify a specific off-centre grasp point (such as a tool's
handle or rim) or select the candidate nearer the arm's measured yaw. Jaws closing along the long axis of an
elongated object rarely lift it. Before releasing an object that requires a target yaw or a 3D posture transition
(such as standing a lying tube/pen upright via source_posture:'lying', target_posture:'upright'), call
pose_plan(request={kind:'place', ...}) for the release yaw and full 3D release_angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw], and
lower close to the support before opening.

items.held_perception: Object-table rows with quality held_fk_depth are candidate held-object geometry estimates, conditioned on rigid attachment to the gripper. A closed jaw or a carried pre-grasp row does not confirm retention. The held entry distinguishes a current mask from prediction_only; even a current mask is not a co-motion check. Use existing RGB and action evidence to assess actual retention, slip and support before relying on the predicted pose.
items.operation_verification: Use Sol operation_verify to verify the full operation at meaningful manipulation outcomes: approach when target alignment is uncertain, grasp and short lift before committing to transfer, the transfer outcome, and placement, release and retreat outcomes. Do not leave verification unused or substitute your own confidence or a completed command for Sol's review. You may combine adjacent caller-chosen moves in one checkpoint when their intermediate outcomes would not change your next decision; supply their actual action IDs in execution order and frame the expected visible result around that checkpoint. Skip a truly irrelevant phase with a brief reason in your task plan; choose checkpoints according to the actual operation, not a fixed phase sequence. Supply saved BEFORE/AFTER RGB, the visible target and intended visible result. Sol verifies evidence and gives feedback; you remain the action planner and choose recovery. Inspect both the model assessment and execution status: visual met does not make a failed/unknown command completed, and a completed receipt does not prove grasp or task success. On uncertainty or failure, resolve the missing evidence or choose a changed recovery; do not loop reviews on unchanged images. Budget reviews together with actor and compaction calls under the shared total model-call budget; combine useful adjacent checkpoints and prioritize unresolved outcomes instead of exhausting the budget on repeated reviews.
